name: Earth Crisis
label: Victory
lede: A Syracuse skater spent three years finding four other vegans who didn't drink, then helped invent metalcore with them and carried vegan straight edge onto 48 Hours, CNN and, eventually, Geraldo.

eras.title: Looking for vegans in Syracuse
eras.text: Syracuse in a recession, friends lost to drugs, and a teenage skater who swore off all of it. Karl Buechner's first Earth Crisis fell apart after a few shows; the second one was built out of another vegan straight edge band, Framework.

years.h: Karl Buechner and DJ Rose start Earth Crisis in Syracuse
years.p: Buechner, on bass, pitches the band to fellow skater DJ Rose, who sings. With Jesse Buckley on drums and John Moseman on guitar, the first Earth Crisis plays a few shows and folds.

q: took me from age 18 to age 21 to get a lineup together
years.h: Karl Buechner takes the mic and raids the band Framework
years.p: Buechner switches to vocals and recruits Framework's Scott Crouse and Ben Read on guitars, Ian "Bulldog" Edwards on bass and Michael Riccardi on drums.
years.xp: Buechner says it took him from 18 to 21 to find a line-up in which every member was vegan and straight edge. He had gone straight edge at about 15, watching friends struggle with drugs during Syracuse's recession, and vegan by around 18.

years.h: All Out War, Earth Crisis's first EP
years.p: Earth Crisis's debut 7" sets out the band's agenda, straight edge and animal liberation, a year before Victory Records comes calling.

eras.title: The demo that went out the car window
eras.text: Victory's Tony Brummel threw away their tape, then saw them play and changed his mind. Firestorm got them argued about across hardcore, Destroy the Machines fused it with metal, and the band ended up explaining veganism on network TV.

years.h: Dennis Merrick and Kris Wiechmann join Earth Crisis
years.p: Merrick replaces Michael Riccardi on drums and Wiechmann replaces Ben Read on guitar. With Buechner, Crouse and Ian Edwards, it's the core that plays on every record to come.

years.src: Decibel (Straight Edge book excerpt) · Wikipedia: Karl Buechner
years.h: Tony Brummel tosses Earth Crisis's tape, then signs them
years.p: According to DJ Rose, Victory Records founder Tony Brummel threw an Earth Crisis tape out his car window unheard. After seeing them at Ohio's More Than Music festival in 1993, he wanted to release their record.
years.xp: Buechner quit college, two years into a history education degree, once Victory signed the band.

years.h: Firestorm EP on Victory, and the scene explodes
years.p: Fifteen minutes on Victory Records, with Firestorm, Forged in the Flames, Eden's Demise and Unseen Holocaust. Greg Bennick of Trial recalls Maximum Rocknroll and others getting upset.
years.xp:
Buechner has said the title song drew on Black Panther writing about communities fighting organized crime and drugs. Critics read it as a call to violence. Other bands, including Demian Johnston of Undertow, objected to the anti-abortion stance in some Earth Crisis songs.

DJ Rose has stressed that Earth Crisis were vegan straight edge, not part of the stricter hardline movement they were often lumped in with.

years.h: Destroy the Machines, Earth Crisis's first album
years.p: Recorded in late 1994 at Believer's studio in Pennsylvania, the album welds New York hardcore to thrash grooves. NME later named it one of the 15 best hardcore punk albums ever.
years.xp: Kerrang! and Loudwire both put it among the best metalcore albums of all time, Loudwire at number 7. [[Between the Buried and Me|1870fb43-50f1-4660-a879-bb596d1519b6]] covered Forced March in 2006. On the 1995 tour, Buechner was caring for rescued animals on the road.

years.h: Karl Buechner starts Path of Resistance while the drummer heals
years.p: With Earth Crisis's drummer out injured, Buechner forms the side band Path of Resistance, which runs until 2006.

years.h: Earth Crisis on MTV, 48 Hours and CNN
years.p: DJ Rose recalls the band appearing on MTV's Smashed, CBS's 48 Hours and CNN's Network Earth, aiming the vegan straight edge message at mainstream viewers.

years.h: Gomorrah's Season Ends, the second Victory album
years.p: Earth Crisis's second full-length for Victory Records, before a jump to a bigger metal label.

eras.title: Roadrunner, and a hometown goodbye
eras.text: Earth Crisis took one shot at a big metal label, with Machine Head's singer as a guest, then went back to Victory. They called it off on good terms at Syracuse's Hellfest.

years.h: Erick Edwards replaces Kris Wiechmann on guitar
years.p: Erick Edwards, brother of bassist Ian Edwards, takes the second guitar spot in Earth Crisis.

years.h: Breed the Killers, Earth Crisis's only Roadrunner album
years.p: Produced by [[Andy Sneap|2b9aed4d-769e-4c38-96e4-586ac59ce668]] at Pyramid Studios in Ithaca, New York, with Robb Flynn of [[Machine Head|22a1f4d7-81ff-4216-ac06-3387da6bc118]] singing on One Against All. It's the band's major-label debut, and its only Roadrunner release.
Earth Crisis returns to Victory Records for its fourth studio album.

years.h: Last of the Sane, the last album of the first run
years.p: Earth Crisis's final Victory album before the break.

years.h: Earth Crisis plays its last show at Hellfest in Syracuse
years.p: The band splits on good terms, citing members' personal commitments. Karl Buechner starts the metal band Freya the same year.

eras.title: Defending the edge, then coming back
eras.text: Karl Buechner became straight edge's spokesman on cable news when the movement was being called a gang. Two years later Earth Crisis was back, with the same five men and three more albums.

years.big: A footnote to the straight edge story
q: it's a tragic end on both sides
years.h: Karl Buechner defends straight edge on Geraldo
years.p: After Utah and Nevada authorities labeled straight edge a gang over assaults in Reno and a Salt Lake City murder case, Buechner went on Fox News' At Large with Geraldo Rivera to argue the violent cases were rare.
years.xp: Buechner told the show straight edge had existed for 25 years with tens of thousands of law-abiding adherents, and called the attacks a footnote to the overall story. He noted the police officer on the panel agreed about 90 percent of straight edgers were peaceful.

years.h: Earth Crisis reunites at the Maryland Metal and Hardcore Festival
years.p: The Breed the Killers-era five come back and keep going: To the Death (2009) and Neutralize the Threat (2011) on Century Media, then Salvation of Innocents (2014) on Candlelight.

Buechner marks the anniversary still fronting Earth Crisis, Freya and Apocalypse Tribe, with shows booked for This Is Hardcore. [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]]'s [[Jamey Jasta|2ae17f26-c50c-4b3b-ac2d-ed5293c03e6c]] is among the singers who cite him as an influence.
The HardLore podcast sits down with Buechner for nearly three hours on Earth Crisis's history, including where the wrench logo came from. He's now also writing science fiction and fantasy.
